To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we engineered a Sar1 variant with improved solution behavior and crystallizability by removing a patch of hydrophilic residues from the N-terminal region.
the aggregation of full-length hamster SAR1 in solution is caused by an N-terminal region of the protein that contains a hydrophobic patch of amino acids.
truncation of the N-terminal nine residues of hamster Sar1 resulted in a Sar1 variant with a monodisperse solution behavior and that this Sar1 variant yielded well diffracting crystals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and characterization of Sar1 variants for crystallization studies.
the crystallization of the small GTPase Sarl, which is an important and novel GTPase that is involved in vesicle trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum.
the design and characterization of a Sar1 variant for crystallization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-terminal region is responsible for the aggregation of full length Sar1.
the N-terminal region is not required for the GTPase activity of Sar1, but it does contribute to the stability and crystallizability of Sar1 in the solution state.
the first nine N-terminal residues of hamster Sar1 are responsible for its aggregation in solution, and the removal of these residues led to a well behaved Sar1 that yielded crystals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-terminal residues in Sar1 are not required for Sar1 function, but do appear to be required for the protein to aggregate in solution.
the N-terminal nine residues in the Sar1 sequence are important for aggregation in solution.
truncating the N-terminal region to remove the patch of hydrophobes was sufficient to improve the protein crystallizability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
truncation of the N-termini of GTPases can improve their crystallizability.
truncation of the N-terminally located hydrophobic patch of Sar1 can improve protein crystallizibility.
